k231:
Durrës city centre — the boulevard, Vollga, Taulantia and Currila — is where people live all year round and where prices are the highest in the city: 1,900–2,800 €/m² (2026-H1) for apartments and above 3,000 €/m² for penthouses with a sea view. Currila has risen 70–90% since 2019.

In the catalogue: 1+1 and 2+1 apartments in new blocks near the promenade, renovated flats in the centre’s older stock, commercial property and offices. For a buyer looking for a city rather than a holiday, this is the zone: the amphitheatre, the port, the station and schools are all within walking distance.

For a lower budget, look at Shkozet and Rrashbull inside the city, or at Plazh along the sea.

k236:
Lalzit Bay stretches north of Durrës, from Cape Rodon to Lalzit beach, with pine forest and gated complexes with private beaches. Asking prices on the second line and in the early construction phases are 1,500–1,700 €/m² (2026-H1), while the bay's large residences ask 2,500–3,500 €/m².

The supply here differs from the rest of Durrës: private villas with land, apartments in managed complexes with a pool, and farmland near Cape Rodon for long-term investment. Tirana is about 40 minutes away, so the area is bought as a second home by residents of the capital.

For cheaper apartments, see Plazh and Shkëmbi i Kavajës south of the city.

k252:
Golem (Kavajë municipality, but part of the Durrës coast as far as the market is concerned) has the largest number of new builds on this coast. Asking prices on the second and third line are 1,100–1,500 €/m² (2026-H1), up 8–15% in a year; the first line, where nothing new is being built, asks 2,000–2,500 €/m² and rises faster still, because supply there does not grow.

Typical offer: studios and 1+1 apartments of 40–60 m² in complexes with a pool and management, and 2+1 apartments of 70–90 m² for families, often priced per m² with instalments during construction. Always ask for the construction stage, the handover date and the ownership certificate — all three are noted on every listing of ours.

For lower prices see neighbouring Mali i Robit; for villas and land, Qerret and Gjiri i Lalzit.

Kavaja sits a few kilometres inland from the coast, on the Durrës–Rrogozhinë road, and lives all year round: railway, market, schools, health centre. Golem, Mali i Robit and Qerret are its beaches, but prices in town are a different market from the first line — lower for the same floor area, without the sea-view premium.

In the catalog: 1+1 and 2+1 apartments in town, private houses with land in the surrounding villages, warehouses and commercial buildings along the main road and at the entrance to town, plots for construction. For this area we do not yet have price series from independent sources, so use the asking prices in the listings as a guide.

For the beach, look at Golem and Qerret, ten minutes away by car.

k304:
Mali i Robit lies between Golem and Qerret, at the foot of the pine-covered hill. Asking prices are 950–1,200 €/m² (2026-H1) — below Golem and well below Qerret — because the area is smaller, has fewer services and no new supply on the first line. For a buyer on a limited budget who wants the sea within 100 metres, this is the most sensible choice on this stretch of coast.

In the catalog: studios and 1+1 apartments in new developments, 2+1 units for families, often priced per m² with instalments during construction. Price data for this area comes only from listings, not from agency series, so we treat it as indicative.

See also neighbouring Golem for a wider choice and Qerret for villas.
